svg.title: From a use case to the mail servers
svg.desc: The path from a use case to the mail servers, from top to bottom. A use case in service calls authorize, and then mailBackend asks the BackendCache for the backend of the account. The BackendCache, in service/backends.go, has one slot for each account. On each call it makes a fingerprint, a SHA-256 hash of the server settings, the key version and the sealed password. With the same fingerprint, it reuses the backend. With a different one, it builds a backend again, and the old backend is retired and closes after 2 minutes. A backend that nobody used for 30 minutes is closed by SweepIdle. The cache gives one imapsmtp.Backend for each account, made by imapsmtp.New. The backend has two paths. On the left, reads, changes and drafts go through the pool in pool.go, which has 2 slots: a call holds one slot and one connection, a stuck connection is closed by force, a call is tried again once if the connection failed, and there is no retry for APPEND, CREATE or the change step of a move. The pool uses the secure dialer in tlsdial.go: it checks the settings, dials within 15 seconds, needs TLS 1.2 or newer, upgrades with STARTTLS and has no fall back to plain text, accepts a pin that is the SHA-256 of the leaf certificate, and then sends the IMAP LOGIN. The dialer connects to the IMAP server. On the right, a send goes through Send in smtp.go, which makes a new SMTP connection for each message, uses AUTH PLAIN only, is all or nothing for the recipients, and then saves the Sent copy through the pool. The SMTP connection has the same rules as the dialer: it checks the settings, connects within 15 seconds (with the handshake in the mode tls), needs TLS 1.2 or newer, upgrades with STARTTLS and has no fall back to plain text, uses the pin PinnedSMTPCert, and then sends AUTH PLAIN. It connects to the SMTP server. A dashed arrow from Send to the pool is the copy of the sent message to the Sent folder.
